title: Information Technology Act, 2000 — Section 5 (Legal Recognition of Electronic Signatures)

content.overview: Section 5 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 gives legal recognition to electronic signatures. Where any law requires a signature, or provides for consequences of an unsigned document, that requirement is deemed satisfied if the document is authenticated by means of an electronic signature in such manner as may be prescribed by the Central Government.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Does a law require a signature? (2) Is authentication by electronic signature as prescribed? (3) Link to ss. 3/3A technique?
content.study:
s. 5 is the signature-side functional equivalence companion to s. 4. Technique still comes from ss. 3/3A.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Signature equivalence
sections.body: A legal requirement of signature is deemed satisfied by authentication by electronic signature in the prescribed manner.

sections.heading: Unsigned-document consequences
sections.body: Where law attaches consequences to an unsigned document, electronic-signature authentication may satisfy the signature element as the section provides.

sections.heading: Prescribed manner
sections.body: Authentication must be in the manner prescribed by the Central Government.

sections.heading: Link to ss. 3/3A
sections.body: Electronic signature technique is governed by ss. 3 and 3A; s. 5 supplies legal recognition of that authentication for signature requirements.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify signature requirement; confirm electronic-signature technique and prescription; apply s. 5 deeming effect.

examples.title: Signed electronic agreement
examples.body: A contract that must be signed is authenticated by a compliant electronic signature — s. 5 deems the signature requirement satisfied subject to prescribed manner.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 5 alone prove the technique of authentication?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. s. 5 recognises electronic signatures for legal signature requirements; the technique itself is under ss. 3/3A.

distinctions.title: s. 5 signatures vs s. 4 records
distinctions.left: Signature requirement satisfied by electronic signature.
distinctions.right: Writing requirement satisfied by electronic record.

misconceptions.correction: Authentication must be by electronic signature in the prescribed manner, using a technique recognised under ss. 3/3A.
